title: Farms that grow towards the ceiling
text: {{1}} windowless buildings beside city ring-roads, towers of trays grow beneath pink-purple light, watered by sensors instead of rain. Vertical farms promise {{2}} deliver salads with {{3}} pesticides and {{4}} tiny fraction of the land and water of field farming, and their crops can be sold within hours of harvest. The economics are hard, largely {{5}} the electricity bill dwarfs every other cost, which is {{6}} the industry has clustered where power is cheap and greens are dear. Japan, {{7}} land is scarce and consumers pay a premium for perfection, has become a centre of the trade. The model has found its niche {{8}} the dream of feeding whole cities from their own basements remains some years off.

gaps.explanation: 'A fraction of' — the fixed quantifying phrase.

gaps.explanation: The reason is explained: which is why.
